To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the toxicological effects caused by Cd in mice liver are related to oxidative stress and to a metabolic switch from oxidative phosphorylation (mitochondrial respiration) to aerobic glycolisis.
Cd induces a metabolic switch from oxidative phosphorylation towards aerobic glycolysis in mouse liver, which is accompanied by oxidative stress and immune response.
Cd causes a metabolic shift from oxidative phosphorylation towards aerobic glycolysis in mouse liver and that this metabolic alteration is associated to Cd hepatocarcenogenicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of Cd toxicity in mice, using the systems biology approach.

the development of new tools for the study of toxicological effects of Cd in mice, and with the integration of different omics approaches to provide new information on Cd hepatotoxicity and carcinogenicity, and to understand its mechanisms.
the development of new methodologies for the analysis of the effects of Cd on the liver of mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Cd is a toxic compound that induces oxidative stress, changes in the expression of genes involved in DNA repair, immune response and metal transport, as well as in lipid metabolism, and a metabolic shift from oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria to aerobic glycolisis in the cytosol.
Cd exposure in mice causes a metabolic switch in liver from oxidative phosphorylative to aerobic glycolytic metabolism, that may be the base for the development of Cd hepatocellular carcinoma.

Cd induces metabolic alterations, oxidative stress and inflammatory responses in the mouse liver, which are the bases of Cd hepatocarciogenicity and could be the cause of other diseases, such as diabetes, obesity, atherosclerosis or neurodegenerative diseases, which have also been related to Cd exposure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cd causes a metabolic switch to aerobic glycolisis in mouse liver, that is a hallmark of cancer cells.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of metabolomics with functional genomics is very useful to obtain a holistic understanding of the biological effects caused by Cd.
metabolomic data can provide a better understanding of the biological processes involved in the toxic effects of Cd in mice, in comparison with functional genomics and proteomics.
the integration of metabolomic data with genomic, transcriptome or proteomic results is essential to obtain a holistic knowledge of biological systems and/or their perturbations.
